external_basis.citation: Dugger et al. 2026, Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution 14:1868960
external_basis.published_sampling: Cape Bird was resighted similarly to Royds and Crozier through 2013; regular chick banding and annual resighting ended after 2013 and later effort was intermittent.

primary_performance_year_rule.reason: The three-colony performance index requires comparable Bird sampling. A numerical >=20 Bird breeder threshold cannot by itself restore the regular sampling regime after 2013.

first_breeding_implication.bird_candidate_rule: The separate detection amendment still excludes any 2014 first-breeding event whose candidate set contains BIRD.
first_breeding_implication.2014_roy_d_croz_only: A 2014 event can remain eligible only if its observed candidate set excludes BIRD and all other frozen controls are valid.

geolocator_implication.primary_choice_analysis: The 2016-2018 geolocator censoring does not affect the primary choice analysis because the Bird performance-year rule makes first-breeding seasons after 2014 ineligible.
geolocator_implication.secondary_or_future_models: ROSS_ISLAND_GEOLOCATOR_CENSORING_V1 remains binding for any later analysis that uses 2016-2018 observations.

information_gate: Apply this performance-year restriction before computing both the source-level >=100 and multi-candidate >=50 event counts.
claim_boundary: Do not use intermittent Bird data after 2013 to extend the primary performance time series.
Do not drop Bird from the performance standardization to rescue later years.
Do not substitute a two-colony Royds/Crozier performance contrast for the frozen three-colony index.
The restriction is an observation-design safeguard, not a biological claim about Bird after 2013.
